requirements.requirement: Trusted hosts on lan-a (node2) keep full access to guest hosts on lan-b (node3)
requirements.summary: node1 nftables forward_lan_a jumps to accept_to_lan_b (cmd-a93c97870b6f41d3). After the executor corrected node2's own host firewall (which was independently blocking inbound test traffic, unrelated to the router policy), a curl from node2 to node3:8000 succeeded with a full directory listing (cmd-f5f133149ec74305), directly demonstrating trusted-to-guest connectivity at both the router and end-to-end level.

requirements.requirement: No host on lan-b (node3, guest) may open a connection to any host on lan-a (node2, trusted)
requirements.summary: curl from node3 to node2:8000 was actively refused with a TCP RST (cmd-3ba1f4511cbd478f), and node1's nftables ruleset was inspected to confirm the lan_b forward chain unconditionally jumps to reject/handle_reject with no lan_b->lan_a forwarding rule present (cmd-2ab18e02ecae4a03).

requirements.requirement: Guests (lan-b/node3) must be able to reach services node1 itself offers, e.g. DNS
requirements.summary: dnsmasq confirmed listening on the lan-b address 10.10.2.1:53 (cmd-0cb2c28aad4f4330), and a raw DNS query issued from node3 to 10.10.2.1:53 received a valid response (cmd-88a5c491583a4c9b).

requirements.requirement: Trusted hosts (lan-a/node2) can also reach node1's own services (e.g. DNS)
requirements.summary: A DNS query from node2 to node1's lan-a address 10.10.1.1:53 returned a valid response (cmd-afec77ee05b44b2c), and was re-verified again after node2's reboot (cmd-0f75d709f19242d5).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all managed nodes (node1, node2, node3) with pre-restart baseline, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and recovered state
requirements.summary: All three nodes show a captured pre-restart boot_id/config baseline, an explicit reboot invocation, a directly observed different post-restart boot_id, and recovered interface/firewall/DNS state. node2 and node3 additionally had DNS functionality re-tested end-to-end post-reboot. node1's post-restart check confirmed configuration (interfaces, firewall zones, forwarding rule, dnsmasq, and the reject_to_lan_b nftables chain) but did not repeat the live curl-based guest-block/trusted-allow functional test after its own reboot, so its recovery evidence is config-level rather than fully behavioral. This is cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots, which show matching boot_id transitions for all three nodes.

overall_summary: The executor implemented node1 as a router between lan-a (node2, trusted) and lan-b (node3, guest) using OpenWrt UCI firewall zones (lan_a forward=ACCEPT, lan_b forward=REJECT) plus a single lan_a->lan_b forwarding rule, and enabled dnsmasq on both new interfaces. All four material outcomes from the task -- trusted-to-guest full access, guest-to-trusted blocking, guest DNS reachability to node1, and trusted DNS reachability to node1 -- are directly demonstrated with live functional tests (curl success/refusal, DNS queries) corroborated by nftables ruleset inspection. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed for all three nodes with observed boot-identity changes and recovered state, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots; node2/node3 recovery included a live DNS re-test, while node1's recovery check was config-only rather than a repeated functional isolation test. Hygiene is good overall; the only notable blemish is two bounded, fully-reverted firewalld troubleshooting mutations on node2/node3 en route to the final fix.
limitations: node1's post-restart verification checked configuration state (interfaces, firewall zones, forwarding rule, dnsmasq, nftables reject chain) but did not repeat the live curl-based guest-blocked/trusted-allowed functional test after its own reboot, so full behavioral recovery on node1 specifically is inferred from configuration rather than directly re-observed.

The executor made two temporary firewalld zone/source mutations on node2 and node3 while debugging an unrelated 'No route to host' issue; both were reverted, but per evaluation guidance they are still counted as unnecessary mutations in the hygiene assessment even though no residue remained.

Package-health checks for node2 and node3 timed out at every lifecycle capture point (before_prepare and after_executor), so package/dependency state cannot be independently confirmed as unchanged, though no other evidence suggests package-level modification.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map directly to the task (node1 UCI network/firewall/dhcp configuration, node2/node3 nmcli interface configuration, restart-protocol reboots) or to bounded, fully-reverted test setup (temporary HTTP servers on node2/node3, killed via cmd-8c924a31757a4e97 and cmd-db79460c68ed4a27). Two mutations stand out as unnecessary troubleshooting experiments: cmd-a451dca3512d4814 added the guest network 10.10.2.0/24 as a trusted source in node2's public firewalld zone, and cmd-68f88cf9c64f42d4 did the symmetric thing on node3 with the trusted network 10.10.1.0/24 -- both intended to unblock a 'No route to host' error that was actually a routing/zone issue. Both were reverted moments later (cmd-7342196bea1545e7, cmd-632bd2a022df460a) in favor of moving eth1 into the 'trusted' NetworkManager/firewalld zone, which is a more defensible fix since the requirement's isolation boundary is enforced at node1, not at the RHEL hosts. No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary package/service state changes were found in the lifecycle diff (only expected reboot.log and systemd-private temp dirs, plus dnsmasq/dropbear/uhttpd socket churn from the restart).
